pointers.sentence: So the metaclass settles which fields a form class has, and in what order, as the class is made, and `BaseForm.__init__` gives each instance its data, its initial values and fields of its own to change (`django/forms/forms.py:DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass.__new__`).

`Form` adds only a metaclass; its comment says it is separate to abstract how the fields are specified, the metaclass being purely a convenience for declaring them as attributes (`django/forms/forms.py:Form`).

It takes out every value that is a form field, an instance of `Field` (`django/forms/fields.py:Field`), and puts them back under one key, `"declared_fields"`, in the order the body assigned them; only then is the class made.

So BerthForm has no attribute named ship, and nor has an instance: a field is reached through the instance's `BaseForm.fields`, or by subscription, which gives its bound field (`django/forms/forms.py:DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass.__new__`).

The dictionary is set on the class as both `BaseForm.base_fields` and `BaseForm.declared_fields`, one object; a model form's metaclass then sets the first again, when its `Meta` names a model, from the model's fields and the declared ones (`django/forms/models.py:ModelFormMetaclass.__new__`).

The metaclass is a subclass of `MediaDefiningClass`, which gives each class whose body defines no `media` a property made by `media_property`; on a form, that property gives the widgets' assets, to which an inner `Media` class ordinarily adds its own ([Form assets: `Media`](media.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:MediaDefiningClass`).

The data, the files and the initial values are kept as given, not copied, or are made empty: a `MultiValueDict` for the first two, a dictionary for the third (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).

`BaseForm.add_prefix` joins it to a field's name with a hyphen, `"berth-ship"` for `prefix="berth"`, and every input's name is made by it; `BaseForm.add_initial_prefix` puts `"initial-"` in front, for the hidden input of a field with `Field.show_hidden_initial` (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.add_prefix`).

`BaseForm.auto_id`, unless given, is `"id_%s"`, a pattern the bound field fills with that name to make the input's `"id"` ([`BoundField`: a field in a form](bound-fields.md)) (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.auto_id`).
`BaseForm.use_required_attribute`, true on the class, lets a bound field put `"required"` on the input of a required field (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`).

`BaseForm.__init__` refuses the two together with a `ValueError`; a formset's forms get `use_required_attribute=False` unless its form arguments say otherwise (`django/forms/formsets.py:BaseFormSet._construct_form`).
`BaseForm.bound_field_class` is the one passed in, else the class's, else the renderer's; a field's own comes before all three (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.get_bound_field`).

An instance's `BaseForm.fields` is a `copy.deepcopy` of its class's `BaseForm.base_fields`, and the comment at the copy says why: those are the definition for the whole class, an instance may want to change its fields, and so it is given its own (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).

Each field is copied by `Field.__deepcopy__`, which copies less than its name says: the copy is shallow but for its widget, its dictionary of messages and its list of validators (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.__deepcopy__`).
`Widget.__deepcopy__` is shallow too, but for a copy of `Widget.attrs` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.__deepcopy__`).

The names listed come first, in that order; a name the form lacks is skipped, which the docstring says lets a subclass remove a field without restating the order; the rest follow in the order they had (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.order_fields`).

`BaseForm.__getitem__` looks a name up in the instance's fields, raising a `KeyError` that lists the names there are, and answers with the field's bound field, made by `Field.get_bound_field` the first time and then kept (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__getitem__`, `django/forms/fields.py:Field.get_bound_field`).

`BaseForm.get_initial_for_field` is what a bound field asks for its initial value (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.get_initial_for_field`).
